1.1: The word of the Lord that came unto Hosea the sonne of Beeri, in the daies of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah Kings of Judah, and in the daies of Jeroboam the sonne of Joash king of Israel.
1.2: At the beginning the Lord spake by Hosea, and the Lord said unto Hosea, Goe, take unto thee a wife of fornications, and children of fornications: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the Lord.
1.3: So he went, and took Gomer, ye daughter of Diblaim, which conceived and bare him a sonne.
1.4: And the Lord said unto him, Cal his name Izreel: for yet a litle, and I will visit the blood of Izreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
1.5: And at that day will I also break the bow of Israel in the valley of Izreel.
1.6: She conceived yet again, and bare a daughter, and God said unto him, Call her name Lo-ruhamah: for I will no more have pitie upon the house of Israel: but I wil utterly take them away.
1.7: Yet I will have mercie upon the house of Judah, and wil save them by the Lord their God, and wil not save them by bow, nor by sword nor by battell, by horses, nor by horsemen.
1.8: Now when she had wained Lo-ruhamah, she conceived, and bare a sonne.
1.9: Then said God, Call his name Lo-ammi: for yee are not my people: therefore will I not be yours.
1.10: Yet the nomber of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which can not be measured nor told: and in the place where it was said unto them, Yee are not my people, it shall be said unto them, Yee are the sonnes of the living God.
1.11: Then shall the children of Judah, and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint them selves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great is the day of Izreel.

2.1: Say unto your brethren, Ammi, and to your sisters, Ruhamah,
2.2: Plead with your mother: plead with her: for she is not my wife, neither am I her husband: but let her take away her fornications out of her sight, and her adulteries from between her breasts.
2.3: Lest I strip her naked, and set her as in the day that she was borne, and make her as a wildernes, and leave her like a drie land, and slaie her for thirst.
2.4: And I wil have no pitie upon her children: for they be the children of fornications.
2.5: For their mother hath plaied the harlot: she that conceived them, hath done shamefully: for she said, I will goe after my lovers that give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, mine oyle and my drink.
2.6: Therefore behold, I will stoop thy way with thornes, and make an hedge, that she shall not find her pathes.
2.7: Though she follow after her lovers, yet shall she not come at them: though she seek them, yet shall she not find them: then shall she say, I will goe and return to my first husband: for at that time was I better then now.
2.8: Now she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oyle, and multiplied her silver and gold, which they bestowed upon Baal.
2.9: Therefore wil I return, and take away my corn in the time thereof, and my wine in the season thereof, and will recover my wool and my flax lent, to cover her shame.
2.10: And now will I discover her lewdnes in the sight of her lovers, and no man shall deliver her out of mine hand.
2.11: I will also cause all her mirth to cease, her feast daies, her new moones, and her Sabbathes, and all her solemn feasts.
2.12: And I wil destroy her vines and her figtrees, whereof she hath said, These are my rewards that my lovers have given mee: and I will make them as a forest, and the wild beasts shall eat them.
2.13: And I wil visit upon her the daies of Baalim, wherein she burnt incense to them: and she decked her self with her earings and her jewels, and she folowed her lovers, and forgat me, saith the Lord.
2.14: Therefore behold, I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak friendly unto her.
2.15: And I will give her her vineyardes from thence, and the valley of Achor for the door of hope, and she shall sing there as in the daies of her youth, and as in the daies when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
2.16: And at that day, sayeth the Lord, thou shalt call me Ishi, and shalt call me no more Baali.
2.17: For I will take away the names of Baalim out of her mouth, and they shall be no more remembred by their names.
2.18: And in that day wil I make a covenant for them, with the wild beasts, and with the foules of the heaven, and with that that creepeth upon the earth: and I will break the bow, and the sword and the battell out of the earth, and will make them to sleep safely.
2.19: And I wil marry thee unto me for ever: yea, I will marry thee unto me in righteousnes, and in iudgement, and in mercy and in compassion.
2.20: I will even marry thee unto me in faithfulnes, and thou shalt know the Lord.
2.21: And in that day I wil hear, saith the Lord, I will even hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth,
2.22: And the earth shall hear the corn, and the wine, and the oyle, and they shall hear Izreel.
2.23: And I will sow her unto me in the earth, and I will have mercie upon her, that was not pitied, and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people. And they shall say, Thou art my God.

3.1: Then said the Lord to me, Goe yet, and love a woman (beloved of her husband, and was an harlot) according to the love of the Lord toward the children of Israel: yet they looked to other gods, and loved the wine bottels.
3.2: So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barlie and an half homer of barlie.
3.3: And I said unto her, Thou shalt abide with me many dayes: thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt be to none other man, and I will be so unto thee.
3.4: For the children of Israel shall remain many dayes without a King and without a prince, and without an offering, and without an image, and without an Ephod and without Teraphim.
3.5: Afterward shall the children of Israel convert, and seek the Lord their God, and David their King, and shall fear the Lord, and his goodnes in the latter dayes.

4.1: Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controuersie with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no trueth nor mercie nor knowledge of God in the land.
4.2: By swearing, and lying, and killing, and stealing, and whoring they break out, and blood toucheth blood.
4.3: Therefore shall the land mourn, and every one that dwelleth therein, shall be cut off, with the beasts of the field, and with the foules of the heaven, and also the fishes of the sea shall be taken away.
4.4: Yet let none rebuke, nor reprove another: for thy people are as they that rebuke the Priest.
4.5: Therefore shalt thou fall in the day, and the Prophet shall fall with thee in the night, and I will destroy thy mother.
4.6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast refused knowledge, I will also refuse thee, that thou shalt be no Priest to me: and seeing thou hast forgotten the Law of thy God, I will also forget thy children.
4.7: As they were increased, so they sinned against me: therefore will I chaunge their glorie into shame.
4.8: They eat up the sinnes of my people, and lift up their mindes in their iniquitie.
4.9: And there shalbe like people, like Priest: for I wil visit their wayes upon them, and reward them their deedes.
4.10: For they shall eat, and not have ynough: they shall commit adulterie, and shall not increase, because they have left off to take heed to ye Lord.
4.11: Whoredom, and wine, and new wine take away their heart.
4.12: My people ask counsel at their stockes, and their staff teacheth them: for the spirit of fornications hath caused them to ere, and they have gone a whoring from under their God.
4.13: They sacrifice upon the toppes of ye mountaines, and burn incense upon the hilles under the okes, and the poplar tree, and the elme, because the shadow thereof is good: therefore your daughters shall be harlots, and your spouses shall be whores.
4.14: I will not visit your daughters when they are harlots: nor your spouses when they are whores: for they themselves are separated with harlots, and sacrifice with whores: therefore the people that doeth not understand, shall fall.
4.15: Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah sinne: come not ye unto Gilgal, neither goe ye up to Beth-aven, nor swear, The Lord liveth.
4.16: For Israel is rebellious as an unruly heyfer. Now the Lord will feed them as a lamb in a large place.
4.17: Ephraim is ioyned to idoles: let him alone.
4.18: Their drunkennes stinketh: they have committed whoredom: their rulers love to say with shame, Bring ye.
4.19: The wind hath bound them up in her wings, and they shalbe ashamed of their sacrifices.

5.1: O ye Priestes, hear this, and hearken ye, O house of Israel, and give ye ear, O house of the King: for iudgement is toward you, because you have been a snare on Mizpah, and a net spred upon Tabor.
5.2: Yet they were profound, to decline to slaughter, though I have been a rebuker of them all.
5.3: I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hid from me: for now, O Ephraim thou art become an harlot, and Israel is defiled.
5.4: They will not give their mindes to turn unto their God: for the spirit of fornication is in the middes of them, and they have not knowen the Lord.
5.5: And the pride of Israel doth testifie to his face: therefore shall Israel and Ephraim fall in their iniquitie: Judah also shall fall with them.
5.6: They shall goe with their sheep, and with their bullockes to seek the Lord: but they shall not find him: for he hath withdrawn himself from them.
5.7: They have transgressed against the Lord: for they have begotte strange children: now shall a moneth deuoure them with their portions.
5.8: Blow ye the trumpet in Gibeah, and the shaume in Ramah: crie out at Beth-aven, after thee, O Beniamin.
5.9: Ephraim shall be desolate in the day of rebuke: among the tribes of Israel have I caused to know the trueth.
5.10: The princes of Judah were like them that remove the bound: therefore will I powre out my wrath upon them like water.
5.11: Ephraim is oppressed, and broken in iudgement, because he willingly walked after the commandement.
5.12: Therefore wil I be unto Ephraim as a moth, and to the house of Judah as a rottenness.
5.13: When Ephraim saw his sickenes, and Judah his wound, then went Ephraim unto Asshur, and sent unto King Jareb: yet could hee not heal you, nor cure you of your wound.
5.14: For I will be unto Ephraim as a lyon, and as a lyons whelp to the house of Judah: I, even I will spoyle, and goe away: I will take away, and none shall rescue it.
5.15: I will go, and return to my place, til they acknowledge their fault, and seek me: in their affliction they will seek me diligently.

6.1: Come, and let us return to the Lord: for he hath spoyled, and he will heal us: he hath wounded us, and he will bind us up.
6.2: After two dayes will he revive us, and in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.
6.3: Then shall we have knowledge, and indeuour our selves to know the Lord: his going forth is prepared as the morning, and he shall come unto us as the rain, and as the latter rain unto the earth.
6.4: O Ephraim, what shall I doe unto thee? O Judah, how shall I intreat thee? for your goodness is as a morning cloud, and as the morning dew it goeth away.
6.5: Therefore have I cut down by the Prophets: I have slain them by the wordes of my mouth, and thy iudgements were as the light that goeth forth.
6.6: For I desired mercie, and not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God more then burnt offrings.
6.7: But they like men have transgressed the covenant: there have they trespassed against me.
6.8: Gilead is a citie of them that work iniquitie, and is polluted with blood.
6.9: And as the eues wait for a man, so the companie of Priestes murder in the way by consent: for they work mischief.
6.10: I have seen vileny in the house of Israel: there is ye whoredom of Ephraim: Israel is defiled.
6.11: Yea, Judah hath set a plant for thee, whiles I would return ye captiuitie of my people.

7.1: When I would have healed Israel, then the iniquitie of Ephraim was discovered, and the wickedness of Samaria: for they have dealt falsly: and the theefe cometh in, and the robber spoyleth without.
7.2: And they consider not in their hearts, that I remember all their wickednes: now their own inventions have beset them about: they are in my sight.
7.3: They make the King glad with their wickedness, and the princes with their lies.
7.4: They are all adulterers, and as a very oven heated by ye baker, which ceaseth from raysing up, and from kneading ye dough until it be leavened.
7.5: This is the day of our King: the princes have made him sick with flagons of wine: he stretcheth out his hand to scorners.
7.6: For they have made ready their heart like an oven whiles they lie in wait: their baker sleepeth all the night: in the morning it burneth as a flame of fire.
7.7: They are all hot as an oven, and have deuoured their judges: all their Kings are fallen: there is none among them that calleth unto me.
7.8: Ephraim hath mixt himself among the people. Ephraim is as a cake on the hearth not turned.
7.9: Strangers have deuoured his strength, and he knoweth it not: yea, gray heares are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not.
7.10: And the pride of Israel testifieth to his face, and they doe not return to the Lord their God, nor seek him for all this.
7.11: Ephraim also is like a dove deceived, without heart: they call to Egypt: they go to Asshur.
7.12: But when they shall go, I will spred my net upon them, and draw them down as the foules of the heaven: I will chastice them as their congregation hath heard.
7.13: Wo unto them: for they have fled away from me: destruction shalbe unto them, because they have transgressed against me: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lyes against me.
7.14: And they have not cryed unto me with their hearts, when they houled upon their beds: they assembled themselves for corn, and wine, and they rebel against me.
7.15: Though I have boud and strengthened their arm, yet doe they imagine mischief against me.
7.16: They return, but not to the most high: they are like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword, for the rage of their tongues: this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.

8.1: Set the trumpet to thy mouth: he shall come as an eagle against the House of the Lord, because they have transgressed my covenant, and trespassed against my Law.
8.2: Israel shall crie unto me, My God, we know thee.
8.3: Israel hath cast off ye thing that is good: the enemie shall pursue him.
8.4: They have set up a King, but not by me: they have made princes, and I knew it not: of their silver and their gold have they made them idoles: therefore shall they be destroyed.
8.5: Thy calf, O Samaria, hath cast thee off: mine anger is kindled against them: how long will they be without innocencie!
8.6: For it came even from Israel: the workeman made it, therefore it is not God: but the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.
8.7: For they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlewind: it hath no stalk: the budde shall bring foorth no meal: if so be it bring forth, the strangers shall deuoure it.
8.8: Israel is deuoured, now shall they be among the Gentiles as a vessell wherein is no pleasure.
8.9: For they are gone up to Asshur: they are as a wild ass alone by himself: Ephraim hath hired lovers.
8.10: Yet though they have hired among the nations, now will I gather them, and they shall sorowe a litle, for the burden of the King and the princes.
8.11: Because Ephraim hath made many altars to sinne, his altars shalbe to sinne.
8.12: I have written to them the great things of my Law: but they were counted as a strange thing.
8.13: They sacrifice flesh for ye sacrifices of mine offerings, and eat it: but the Lord accepteth them not: now will he remember their iniquitie, and visit their sinnes: they shall return to Egypt.
8.14: For Israel hath forgotten his maker, and buildeth Temples, and Judah hath increased strong cities: but I will send a fire upon his cities, and it shall deuoure the palaces thereof.

9.1: Rejoice not, O Israel for joy as other people: for thou hast gone a whoring from thy God: thou hast loved a reward upon every corn floor.
9.2: The floor, and the wine press shall not feed them, and the new wine shall fail in her.
9.3: They wil not dwel in the Lordes land, but Ephraim will return to Egypt, and they will eat vncleane things in Asshur.
9.4: They shall not offer wine to the Lord, neither shall their sacrifices be pleasant unto him: but they shall be unto them as the bread of mourners: al that eat thereof, shalbe polluted: for their bread for their soules shall not come into the house of the Lord.
9.5: What wil ye do then in the solemn day, and in the day of the feast of the Lord?
9.6: For loe, they are gone from destruction: but Egypt shall gather them up, and Memphis shall burie them: the nettle shall possess the pleasant places of their silver, and the thorn shall be in their tabernacles.
9.7: The daies of visitation are come: the daies of recompence are come: Israel shall know it: the Prophet is a fool: the spiritual man is mad, for the multitude of thine iniquitie: therefore the hatred is great.
9.8: The watchman of Ephraim should bee with my God: but the Prophet is the snare of a fouler in all his waies, and hatred in the House of his God.
9.9: They are deepely set: they are corrupt as in the daies of Gibeah: therefore he will remember their iniquitie, he will visit their sinnes.
9.10: I found Israel like grapes in the wildernes: I saw your fathers as the first ripe in the figge tree at her first time: but they went to Baal-Peor, and separated themselves unto that shame, and their abominations were according to their lovers.
9.11: Ephraim their glorie shall flee away like a bird: from the birth and from the womb, and from the conception.
9.12: Though they bring up their children, yet I will depriue them from being men: yea, woe to them, when I depart from them.
9.13: Ephraim, as I saw, is as a tree in Tyrus planted in a cottage: but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murtherer.
9.14: O Lord, give them: what wilt thou give them? give them a baren womb and drie breasts.
9.15: All their wickedness is in Gilgal: for there doe I hate them: for the wickedness of their inventions, I will cast them out of mine House: I will love them no more: all their princes are rebels.
9.16: Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up: they can bring no fruit: yea, though they bring foorth, yet will I slaie even the dearest of their bodie.
9.17: My God will cast them away, because they did not obey him: and they shall wander among the nations.

10.1: Israel is a emptie vine, yet hath it brought foorth fruit unto it self, and according to the multitude of the fruit thereof he hath increased the altars: according to the goodness of their land they have made fair images.
10.2: Their heart is deuided: now shall they be found faultie: he shall break down their altars: he shall destroy their images.
10.3: For now they shall say, We have no King because we feared not the Lord: and what should a King doe to us?
10.4: They have spoken woordes, swearing falsly in making a covenant: thus iudgement groweth as wormewoode in the furrowes of the field.
10.5: The inhabitants of Samaria shall fear because of the calf of Beth-aven: for the people thereof shall mourn over it, and the Chemarims thereof, that reioyced on it for the glorie thereof, because it is departed from it.
10.6: It shall bee also brought to Asshur, for a present unto King Jareb: Ephraim shall receive shame, and Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel.
10.7: Of Samaria, the King thereof is destroyed as the some upon the water.
10.8: The hie places also of Aven shall be destroied, even the sinne of Israel: the thorn and the thistle shall grow upon their altars, and they shall say to the mountaines, Cover us, and to the hils, Fall upon us.
10.9: O Israel, thou hast sinned from the daies of Gibeah: there they stood: the battell in Gibeah against the children of iniquitie did not touch them.
10.10: It is my desire that I should chastice them, and the people shall be gathered against them, when they shall gather themselves in their two furrowes.
10.11: And Ephraim is as an heifer used to delite in threshing: but I will pass by her fair neck: I will make Ephraim to ride: Judah shall plow, and Iaakob shall break his cloddes.
10.12: Sow to your selves in righteousnes: reap after the measure of mercy: break up your fallow ground: for it is time to seek the Lord, till he come and rain righteousness upon you.
10.13: But you have plowed wickedness: ye have reaped iniquitie: you have eaten the fruit of lies: because thou didest trust in thine own waies, and in the multitude of thy strong men,
10.14: Therefore shall a tumult arise among thy people, and all thy munitions shall be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth-arbell in the daie of battell: the mother with the children was dashed in pieces.
10.15: So shall Beth-el doe unto you, because of your malicious wickednes: in a morning shall the King of Israel be destroied.

11.1: When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my sonne out of Egypt.
11.2: They called them, but they went thus from them: they sacrificed unto Baalim, and burnt incense to images.
11.3: I ledde Ephraim also, as one should bear them in his armes: but they knew not that I healed them.
11.4: I led them with cordes of a man, even with bandes of love, and I was to them, as hee that taketh off the yoke from their iawes, and I laid the meat unto them.
11.5: He shall no more return into the land of Egypt: but Asshur shalbe his King, because they refused to convert.
11.6: And the sword shall fall on his cities, and shall consume his barres, and deuoure them, because of their own counsels.
11.7: And my people are bent to rebellion against me: though they called them to the most hie, yet none at all would exalt him.
11.8: How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel? how shall I make thee, as Admah? how shall I set thee, as Zeboim? mine heart is turned within mee: my repentings are rouled together.
11.9: I wil not execute ye fierceness of my wrath: I will not return to destroy Ephraim: for I am God, and not man, the holy one in the middes of thee, and I will not enter into the citie.
11.10: They shall walk after the Lord: he shall roar like a lyon: when hee shall roar, then the children of the West shall fear.
11.11: They shall fear as a sparrow out of Egypt, and as a dove of the land of Asshur, and I will place them in their houses, sayth the Lord.
11.12: Ephraim copasseth me about with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit: but Judah yet ruleth with God, and is faithful with the Saints.

12.1: Ephraim is fed with the wind, and followeth after the East wind: hee increaseth daily lies and destruction, and they do make a covenant with Asshur, and oyle is caried into Egypt.
12.2: The Lord hath also a controuersie with Judah, and will visit Iaakob, according to his waies: according to his workes, wil he recompence him.
12.3: Hee took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with God,
12.4: And had power over the Angel, and prevailed: he wept and praied unto him: he found him in Beth-el, and there he spake with us.
12.5: Yea, the Lord God of hostes, the Lord is himself his memorial.
12.6: Therefore turn thou to thy God: keep mercy and iudgement, and hope still in thy God.
12.7: He is Canaan: the balances of deceit are in his hand: he loveth to oppress.
12.8: And Ephraim said, Notwithstanding I am rich, I have found me out riches in all my labours: they shall find none iniquitie in me, that were wickedness.
12.9: Though I am the Lord thy God, from the land of Egypt, yet will I make thee to dwel in the tabernacles, as in the daies of the solemn feast.
12.10: I have also spoken by the Prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes by the ministerie of the Prophets.
12.11: Is there iniquitie in Gilead? surely they are vanitie: they sacrifice bullocks in Gilgal, and their altars are as heapes in the furrowes of the field.
12.12: And Iaakob fled into the countrey of Aram, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.
12.13: And by a Prophet the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt, and by a Prophet was he reserved.
12.14: But Ephraim provoked him with hie places: therefore shall his blood be powred upon him, and his reproche shall his Lord reward him.

13.1: When Ephraim spake, there was trembling: hee exalted him self in Israel, but he hath sinned in Baal, and is dead.
13.2: And now they sinne more and more, and have made them molten images of their silver, and idoles according to their own understanding: they were all the woorke of the craftesmen: they say one to another whiles they sacrifice a man, Let them kiss the calves.
13.3: Therefore they shall bee as the morning cloud, and as the morning dew that passeth away, as the chaff that is driven with a whirlewind out of the floor, and as the smoke that goeth out of the chimney.
13.4: Yet I am the Lord thy God from the land of Egypt, and thou shalt know no God but me: for there is no Sauiour beside me.
13.5: I did know thee in the wilderness, in the land of drought.
13.6: As in their pastures, so were they filled: they were filled, and their heart was exalted: therefore have they forgotten me.
13.7: And I wil be unto them as a very lyon, and as a leopard in the way of Asshur.
13.8: I will meet them, as a bear that is robbed of her whelpes, and I will break the kall of their heart, and there will I deuoure them like a lion: the wild beast shall tear them.
13.9: O Israel, one hath destroyed thee, but in me is thine help.
13.10: I am: where is thy King, that should help thee in al thy cities? and thy judges, of whom thou saidest, Give me a King, and princes?
13.11: I gave thee a King in mine anger, and I took him away in my wrath.
13.12: The iniquitie of Ephraim is bound up: his sinne is hid.
13.13: The sorowes of a travailing woman shall come upon him: he is an unwise sonne, els would he not stand still at the time, even at the breaking forth of the children.
13.14: I wil redeem them from the power of the grave: I will deliver them from death: O death, I wil be thy death: O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance is hid from mine eyes.
13.15: Though he grew up among his brethren, an East wind shall come, even the wind of the Lord shall come up from the wilderness, and drie up his vein, and his fountain shalbe dryed up: he shall spoyle the treasure of all pleasant vessels.

14.1: Samaria shalbe desolate: for she hath rebelled against her God: they shall fall by the sword: their infants shalbe dashed in pieces, and their women with child shalbe ript.
14.2: O Israel, return unto the Lord thy God: for thou hast fallen by thine iniquitie.
14.3: Take unto you words, and turn to the Lord, and say unto him, Take away all iniquitie, and receive us graciously: so wil we render the calves of our lippes.
14.4: Asshur shall not save us, neither wil we ride upon horses, neither will we say any more to the work of our handes, Ye are our gods: for in thee the fatherless findeth mercie.
14.5: I wil heal their rebellion: I wil love them freely: for mine anger is turned away from him.
14.6: I will be as the dew unto Israel: he shall grow as the lilie and fasten his rootes, as the trees of Lebanon.
14.7: His branches shall spread, and his beautie shalbe as the olive tree, and his smell as Lebanon.
14.8: They that dwel under his shadow, shall return: they shall revive as the corn, and florish as the vine: the sent thereof shalbe as the wine of Lebanon.
14.9: Ephraim shall say, What have I to doe any more with idoles? I have heard him, and looked upon him: I am like a green fire tree: upon me is thy fruit found.
14.10: Who is wise, and he shall vnderstande these things? and prudent, and he shall know them? for the wayes of the Lord are righteous, and the just shall walk in them: but the wicked shall fall therein.

28:1:1: So that it may be gathered by the reign of these four kings, that he preached above threescore years.
Called also Azariah, who being a leper was disposed from his kingdom.
28:1:2: That is, one that of long time hath accustomed to play the harlot: not that the Prophet did this thing in effect, but he saw this in a vision, or else was commanded by God to set forth under this parable or figure the idolatry of the Synagogue, and of the people her children.
28:1:3: Gomer signifieth a consumption or corruption, and Diblaim clusters of figs, declaring that they were all corrupt like rotten figs.
28:1:4: I will be revenged upon Jehu for the blood that he shed in Jezreel: for albeit God stirred him up to execute his judgments, yet he did them for his own ambition, and not for the glory of God as the end declared: for he built up that idolatry which he had destroyed.

Meaning, that they should be no more called Israelites of the which name they boasted because Israel, did prevail with God: but that they were as bastard, and therefore should be called Jezreelites, that is scattered people, alluding to Jezreel, which was the chief city of the ten tribes under Ahab where Jehu shed so much blood, 2 Kings 10:8.
28:1:5: When the measure of their iniquity is full, and I shall take vengeance and destroy all their policy and force.
28:1:6: For the Israelites never returned after that they were taken captives by the Assyrians.
That is, not obtaining mercy: whereby he signifieth, that God’s favor was departed from them.
28:1:7: For after their captivity he restored him miraculously by the means of Cyrus, Ezra 1:1.
28:1:10: Because they thought that God could not have been true in his promise except he had preserved them, he declareth though they were destroyed, yet the true Israelites, which are the sons of the promise, should be without number, which stand both of the Jews and the Gentiles, Rom. 9:26.
28:1:11: To wit, after the captivity of Babylon when the Jews were restored, but chiefly this is referred to the time of Christ, who should be the head both of the Jews and Gentiles.
The calamity and destruction of Israel shall be so great, that to restore them shall be as a miracle.
28:2:1: Seeing that I have promised you deliverance, it remaineth that you encourage one another to embrace the same, considering that ye are my people on whom I will have mercy.
28:2:2: God showeth that the fault was not in him, but in their Synagogue, and their idolatries, that he forsook them, Isa. 50:1.
Meaning, that their idolatry was so great, that they were not ashamed, but boasted of it, Ezek. 16:25.
28:2:3: For though this people were as an harlot for their idolatries, yet he had left them with their apparel and dowry and certain signs of his favor, but if they continued still, he would utterly destroy them.
When I brought her out of Egypt, Ezek. 16:4.
28:2:4: That is, bastards and begotten in adultery.
28:2:5: Meaning, the idol which they served, and by whom they thought they had wealth and abundance.
28:2:6: I will punish thee that then thou mayest try whether thine idols can help thee, and bring thee into such straightness that thou shalt have no lust to play the wanton.
28:2:7: This he speaketh of the faithful, which are truly converted, and also showeth the use and profit of God’s rods.
28:2:8: This declareth that idolaters defraud God of his honor, when they attribute his benefits to their idols.
28:2:9: Signifying, that God will take away his benefits when man by his ingratitude doth abuse them.
28:2:10: That is, all her service, ceremonies and inventions whereby she worshipped her idols.
28:2:13: I will punish her for her idolatry.
By showing how harlots trim themselves to please others, he declareth how that superstitious idolaters set a great part of their religion, in decking themselves on their holy days.
28:2:14: By my benefits in offering her grace and mercy, even in that place where she shall think herself destitute of all help and comfort.
28:2:15: Which was a plentiful valley, and wherein they had great comfort when they came out of the wilderness, as Josh. 7:26, and is called the door of hope, because it was a departing from death and an entry into life.
She shall then praise God as she did when she was delivered out of Egypt.
28:2:16: That is, my master: which name was applied to their idols.
That is, mine husband, knowing that I am joined to thee by an inviolable covenant.
28:2:17: No idolatry shall once come into their mouth, but they shall serve me purely according to my word.
28:2:18: Meaning, that he will so bless them that all creatures shall favor them.
28:2:20: With a covenant that never shall be broken.
28:2:21: Then shall the heaven desire rain for the earth which shall bring forth for the use of man.
28:3:1: That is, gave themselves wholly to pleasure, and could not take up, as they that are given to drunkenness.
Herein the Prophet representeth the person of God, which loved his Church before he called her, and did not withdraw the same when she gave herself to idols.
28:3:2: Yet I loved her and paid a small portion for her, lest she perceiving the greatness of my love, should have abused me, and not been under duty: for fifteen pieces of silver were but half the price of a slave, Exod. 21:32.
28:3:3: I will try thee a long time as in thy widowhood whether thou wilt be mine or no.
28:3:4: That is, they should neither have policy nor religion, and their idols also wherein they put their confidence, should be destroyed.
Meaning, not only all the time of their captivity, but also unto Christ.
28:3:5: This is meant of Christ’s kingdom, which was promised unto David to be eternal, Ps. 72:17.
28:4:1: Because the people would not obey the admonitions of the Prophet, he citeth them before the judgment seat of God, against whom they chiefly offended, Isa. 7:13; Zech. 12:10; Mic. 6:1, 2.
28:4:2: In every place appeareth a liberty to most heinous vices, so that one followeth in the neck of another.
28:4:4: As though he would say that it were in vain to rebuke them: for no man can abide it: yea, they will speak against the prophets and priests whose office it is chiefly to rebuke them.
28:4:5: Ye shall perish all together the one because he would not obey, and the other, because he would not admonish.
That is, the Synagogue wherein thou boastest.
28:4:6: That is, the Priests shall be cast off, because that for lack of knowledge, they are not able to execute their charge, and instruct others, Deut. 33:3; Mal. 2:7.
Meaning, the whole body of the people, which were weary with hearing the word of God.
28:4:7: The more I was beneficial unto them.
28:4:8: To wit, the Priests seek to eat the people’s offerings, and flatter them in their sins.
28:4:9: Signifying, that as they have sinned together, so shall they be punished together.
28:4:10: Showing that their wickedness shall be punished on all sorts: for though they think by the multitude of wives to have many children, yet they shall be deceived of their hope.
28:4:11: In giving themselves to pleasures, they become like brute beasts.
28:4:12: Thus he speaketh by derision in calling them his people, which now for their sins they were not: for they sought help of stocks and sticks.
They are carried away with a rage.
28:4:13: Because they take away God’s honor, and give it to idols: therefore he will give them up to their lusts, that they shall dishonor their own bodies, Rom. 1:28.
28:4:14: I will not correct your shame to bring you to amendment, but let you run headlong to your own damnation.
28:4:15: God complaineth that Judah is infected, and willeth them to learn to return in time.
For albeit the Lord had honored this place in time past by his presence, yet because it was abused by their idolatry, he would not that his people should resort thither.

He calleth Bethel, that is, the house of God, Beth Aven, that is, the house of iniquity, because of their abominations set up there, signifying that no place is holy, where God is not purely worshipped.
28:4:16: God will so disperse them, that they shall not remain in any certain place.
28:4:18: They are so impudent in receiving bribes, that they will command men to bring them unto them.
28:5:1: The Priests and Princes caught the poor people in their snares, as the fowlers did the birds, in these two high mountains.
28:5:2: Notwithstanding they seemed to be given altogether to holiness, and to sacrifices which here he calleth slaughter in contempt.
Though I had admonished them continually by my Prophets.
28:5:3: They boasted themselves not only to be Israelites, but also Ephraimites, because their king Jeroboam came of that tribe.
28:5:5: Meaning, their contemning of all admonitions.
28:5:7: Their destruction is not far off.
That is, their children are degenerate, so that there is no hope in them.
28:5:8: That is, all Israel comprehended under this part, signifying that the Lord’s plagues should pursue them from place to place till they were destroyed.
28:5:9: By the success they shall know that I have surely determined this.
28:5:10: They have turned upside down all political order and all manner of religion.
28:5:11: To wit, after king Jeroboam’s commandment, and did not rather follow God.
28:5:13: Instead of seeking for remedy at God’s hand.
Who was king of the Assyrians.
28:6:1: He showeth the people how they ought to turn to the Lord, that he might call back his plagues.
28:6:2: Though he correct us from time to time, yet his help will not be far off, if we return to him.
28:6:4: You seem to have a certain holiness and repentance, but it is upon the sudden, and as a morning cloud.
28:6:5: My doctrine which I taught thee, was most evident.
I have still labored by my prophets, and as it were framed you to bring you to amendment, but all was in vain: for my word was not food to feed them, but a sword to slay them.
28:6:6: He showeth to what scope his doctrine tended, that they should join the obedience of God, and the love of their neighbor with outward sacrifices.
28:6:7: That is, like light and weak persons.
28:6:8: Which was the place where the Priests dwelt, and which should have been best instructed in my word.
28:6:11: That is, doth imitate thine idolatry, and hath taken grafts of thy trees.
28:7:1: Meaning, that there was no one kind of vice among them, but that they were subject to all wickedness, both secret and open.
28:7:3: They esteem their wicked king Jeroboam above God, and seek but how to flatter and please him.
28:7:4: He compareth the rage of the people to a burning oven which the baker heateth, still till his dough be leavened and raised.
28:7:5: They used all riot and excess in their feasts, and solemnities whereby their king was overcome with surfeit, and brought into diseases, and delighted in flatteries.
28:7:7: By their occasion God hath deprived them of all good rulers.
28:7:8: That is, he counterfeited the religion of the Gentiles, yet is but as a cake baked on the one side, and raw on the other, that is, neither thoroughly hot, nor thoroughly cold, but partly a Jew, and partly a Gentile.
28:7:9: Which are a token of his manifold afflictions.
28:7:11: That is, without all judgment, as they that cannot tell whether it is better to cleave only to God, or to seek the help of man.
28:7:12: According to my curses made to the whole Congregation of Israel.
28:7:13: That is, divers times redeemed them, and delivered them from death.
28:7:14: They only seek their own commodity and wealth, and pass not for me their God.
When they were in affliction, and cried out for pain, they sought not unto me for help.
28:7:16: Because they boast of their own strength, and pass not what they speak against me and my servants, Ps. 73:9.
28:8:1: God encourageth the Prophet to signify the speedy coming of the enemy against Israel, which was once the people of God.
28:8:2: They shall cry like hypocrites, but not from the heart, as their deeds declare.
28:8:4: That is, Jeroboam by whom they sought their own liberty, and not to obey my will.
28:8:5: That is, upright judgment and godly life.
28:8:6: Meaning, the calf was invented by themselves, and of their fathers in the wilderness.
28:8:7: Showing that their religion hath but a show, and in itself is but vanity.
28:8:9: They never cease, but run to and fro to seek help.
28:8:10: That is, for the king and the princes shall lay upon them: which means the Lord useth to bring them to repentance.
28:8:12: Thus the idolaters count the word of God as strange in respect of their own inventions.
28:8:13: Saying that they offer it to the Lord, but he accepteth no service, which he himself hath not appointed.
28:9:1: For though all other people should escape, yet thou shalt be punished.
Thou hast committed idolatry in hope of reward, and to have thy barns filled, Jer. 44:17, as an harlot that had rather live by playing the whore, than to be entertained of her own husband.
28:9:2: These outward things that thou seekest, shall be taken from thee.
28:9:4: The meat offering which they offered for themselves.
All their doings both touching policy and religion, shall be rejected as things polluted.
28:9:5: When the Lord shall take away all the occasions of serving him, which shall be the most grievous point of your captivity, when ye shall see yourselves cut off from God.
28:9:6: Though they think to escape by fleeing the destruction that is at hand, yet shall they be destroyed in the place whither they flee for succor.
28:9:7: Then they shall know that they were deluded by them, who challenged to themselves to be their prophets and spiritual men.
28:9:8: The Prophet’s duty is to bring men to God, and not to be a snare to pull them from God.
28:9:9: This people is so rooted in their wickedness, that Gibeah which was like to Sodom, was never more corrupt, Judg. 19:22.
28:9:10: They were as abominable unto me, as their lovers the idols.
Meaning, that he so esteemed them and delighted in them.
28:9:11: Signifying, that God would destroy their children by these sundry means, and so consume them by little and little.
28:9:13: As they kept tender plants in their houses in Tyre to preserve them from the cold air of the sea, so was Ephraim at the first unto me, but now I will give him to the slaughter.
28:9:14: The Prophet seeing the great plagues of God toward Ephraim, prayeth to God to make them barren, rather than that this great slaughter should come upon their children.
28:9:15: The chief cause of their destruction is that they commit idolatry, and corrupt my Religion in Gilgal.
28:10:1: Whereof though the grapes were gathered, yet ever as it gathered new strength, it increased new wickedness, so that the correction which should have brought them to obedience, did but utter their stubbornness.
As they were rich and had abundance.
28:10:3: The day shall come that God shall take away their king, and then they shall feel the fruit of their sins, and how they trusted in him in vain, 2 Kings 17:6, 7.
28:10:4: Thus their integrity and fidelity, which they pretended, was nothing but bitterness and grief.
In promising to be faithful toward God.
28:10:5: When the calf shall be carried away.
Chemarims were certain idolatrous priests, which did wear black apparel in their sacrifices, and cried with a loud voice: which superstition Elijah derided, 1 Kings 18:27, read 2 Kings 23:5.
28:10:8: This he speaketh in contempt of Bethel, read Hos. 4:15.
28:10:9: The Israelites were not moved by their example to cease from their sins.
In those days wast thou as wicked as the Gibeonites, as God there partly declared: for thy zeal could not be good in executing God’s judgments, seeing thine own deeds were as wicked as theirs.
To wit, to fight, or the Israelites remained in that stubbornness from that time.
28:10:10: Because they are so desperate, I will delight to destroy them.
That is, when they have gathered all their strength together.
28:10:11: I will lay my yoke upon her fat neck.
Wherein is pleasure, as in plowing is labor and pain.
28:10:14: That is, Shalmaneser in the destruction of that city spared neither kind nor age.
28:11:1: While the Israelites were in Egypt, and did not provoke my wrath by their malice and ingratitude.
28:11:2: They rebelled and went a contrary way when the Prophets called them to repentance.
28:11:4: That is, friendly: and not as beasts or slaves.
28:11:5: Seeing they contemn all this kindness, they shall be led captive into Assyria.
28:11:8: God considereth with himself, and that with a certain grief, how to punish them.

Meaning, that his love wherewith he first loved them, made him between doubt and assurance what to do: and herein appeareth his Fatherly affection: that his mercy toward his shall overcome his judgments, as he declareth in the next verse.
Which were two of the cities that were destroyed with Sodom, Deut. 29:23.
28:11:9: To consume thee, but will cause thee to yield, and so receive thee to mercy: and this is meant of the final number who shall walk after the Lord.
28:11:11: The Egyptians, and the Assyrians shall be afraid when the Lord maintaineth his people.
28:11:12: Governeth their state according to God’s word, and doth not degenerate.
28:12:1: That is, flattereth himself with vain confidence.
28:12:2: Which in those points was like to Ephraim, but not in idolatries.
28:12:3: Seeing that God did thus prefer Jacob their father, Judah’s ingratitude was the more to be abhorred.
28:12:4: God found Jacob as he lay sleeping in Bethel, Gen. 28:12, and so spake with him there, that the fruit of that speech appertained to the whole body of the people, whereof we are.
28:12:7: As for Ephraim he is more like the wicked Canaanites, than godly Abraham or Jacob.
28:12:8: Thus the wicked measure God’s favor by outward prosperity and like hypocrites cannot abide that any should reprove their doings.
28:12:9: Seeing thou wilt not acknowledge my benefits, I will bring thee again to dwell in tents, as in the feast of the Tabernacles, which thou dost now contemn.
28:12:11: The people thought that no man durst have spoken against Gilead, that holy place, and yet the Prophet saith, that all their religion was but vanity.
28:12:12: If you boast of your riches and nobility, ye seem to reproach your father, who was a poor fugitive and servant.
28:12:13: Meaning, Moses, whereby appeareth, that whatsoever they have, it cometh of God’s free goodness.
28:13:1: He made a king of his tribe.
He showeth the excellency and authority that this tribe had above all the rest.
The Ephraimites are not far from destruction, and have lost their authority.
28:13:2: The false prophets persuaded the idolaters to offer their children after the example of Abraham, and he showeth how they would exhort one another to the same, and to kiss and worship these calves which were their idols.
28:13:4: He calleth them to repentance, and reproveth their ingratitude.
28:13:9: Thy destruction is certain, and my benefits toward thee declare that it cometh not of me: therefore thine own malice, idolatry and vain confidence in men must needs be the cause thereof.
28:13:12: It is surely laid up to be punished, as Jer. 17:1.
28:13:13: But would come out of the womb, that is out of this dangers wherein he is and not to tarry to be stifled.
28:13:14: Because they will not turn to me, I will change my purpose.
Meaning, that no power shall resist God when he will deliver his, but even in death will he give them life.
28:14:2: He exhorteth them to repentance to avoid all these plagues, willing them to declare by words their obedience and repentance.
28:14:3: Declaring that this is the true sacrifice, that the faithful can offer, even thanks and praise, Heb. 13:15.
He showeth them how they ought to confess their sins.
28:14:4: We will leave off all vain confidence and pride.
28:14:5: He declareth how ready God is to receive them that do repent.
28:14:8: Whosoever join themselves to this people, shall be blessed.
28:14:9: God showeth how prompt he is to hear his, when they repent, and to offer himself, as a protection and safeguard unto them, as a most sufficient fruit and profit.
28:14:10: Signifying, that the true wisdom and knowledge consisteth in this even to rest upon God.
